title: Sachin Tendulkar Invests in Recykal, Extending $23 Million Bridge Round
excerpt: Tendulkar joins the Hyderabad waste-management platform as a strategic investor for an undisclosed amount; Recykal has raised over $60 million and reported ₹1,498 crore FY26 gross revenue.
body:
• Sachin Tendulkar has joined Hyderabad-based Recykal as a strategic investor, in an extension of the waste-management platform's $23 million bridge round closed in June 2026; the size of his investment was not disclosed.
  • The bridge round comprised $17.6 million in equity and a $5.4 million secondary component, according to Inc42; Recykal has raised more than $60 million to date.
  • Recykal reported FY26 gross revenue of ₹1,498 crore, up 53.2% from ₹978 crore a year earlier, with losses edging up to ₹60 crore from ₹56 crore, Inc42 reported.
  • For readers: Recykal is a private company — there is no public share to buy on the back of this news; the investable angle is India's formal recycling and deposit-return systems, not a listed stock.

Former India cricketer Sachin Tendulkar has invested in Recykal, a Hyderabad-based technology platform for waste management and the circular economy, as a strategic investor. His investment extends the $23 million bridge round the company closed in June, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. The company did not disclose how much Tendulkar invested.

What was reported

Recykal said Tendulkar invested during the extension of its recently closed $23 million bridge round, according to Inc42. The June round comprised $17.6 million in equity funding and an additional $5.4 million secondary component, with participation from existing backers and family offices. The bridge round as a whole comprised primary and secondary capital from existing investors and select new family offices, BusinessLine reported.

Tendulkar will help the company in its campaign to make responsible waste behaviour an everyday habit, the company said in a statement on Friday, according to BusinessLine.

"What drew me to Recykal was seeing how technology was being used to solve an everyday problem. Recykal's mission to use technology to drive behavioural change across one billion people is what really connected with me."

— Sachin Tendulkar, strategic investor, Recykal

What Recykal does, and where the money goes

Recykal operates a B2B marketplace for recyclable materials and provides software that helps brands track plastic and e-waste recycling to meet compliance mandates, Inc42 reported. The company is using the bridge capital to strengthen its technology platform and Open Marketplace, scale its Deposit Return System (DRS) and expand into overseas markets, BusinessLine reported. Under DRS, consumers pay a refundable deposit on containers at purchase and get it back when they return the container to a collection point, Inc42 explained. The company also develops AI-enabled hardware such as reverse vending machines.

Recykal claims a network of more than 5,000 waste aggregators and recyclers and says it works with 650 enterprise brands, including Hindustan Unilever, Samsung and BMW. BusinessLine reported the company claimed it had channelled over 30 lakh tonnes of waste through its ecosystem. Its backers include Morgan Stanley, 360 ONE, Circulate Capital and the Murugappa Group, and it has raised more than $60 million in total, according to Inc42.

The numbers behind the platform

Inc42 reported that Recykal closed FY26 with gross revenue of ₹1,498 crore, up 53.2% from ₹978 crore in FY25, while losses rose about 7% to ₹60 crore from ₹56 crore. Those are company-reported figures relayed by Inc42, not audited results published in this coverage. The growth shows scale in a business built on moving recyclable material at volume; the widening loss shows it is not yet profitable.

What to watch next

Two things will test whether Tendulkar's backing translates into business results rather than visibility alone: whether the Deposit Return System expands beyond its current footprint, and whether the overseas expansion funded by the bridge round materialises. For diaspora readers following Indian startups, Recykal remains private, so there is no listed-market action to take on this announcement. The next verifiable milestones are further funding disclosures and any DRS rollout announcements from the company itself.
